Criminal Justice Accused cancer scammer Lexi Thomas arrested in Howard County 
 Julie Scharper 11/19/2026 3:50 p.m. EST , Updated 11/19/2026 6:57 p.m. EST 28 Share Share this via... Subscribe and listen to this story in The Banner app Scan this with your phone’s camera to download Save this story in The Banner app Scan this with your phone’s camera to download Lexi Thomas, a Howard County woman, is accused of faking cancer for more than a decade and raising hundreds of thousands of dollars for her medical bills. ( Courtesy of Dan Goldsmith ) The subject of ‘The Lexi Con’ podcast series is charged with felony theft
 Lexi Thomas, who spent more than a decade chronicling her struggles with what she claimed was cancer and who raised hundreds of thousands of dollars for medical treatment, was arrested Thursday and is being held without bond. 
 A Howard County grand jury indicted Thomas , 34, on two felony charges: theft up to $25,000 and theft up to $10,000. 
 The indictment, which was unsealed Thursday, provides little detail into the charges against Thomas but lists the names of more than two dozen people from whom Thomas allegedly stole.
 Washington attorney Max F. Maccoby, who is listed as representing Thomas in online court records, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
 Advertise with us Her parents, Vernon and Elizabeth Thomas, did not immediately reply to a phone message left at their Montgomery County home. 
 Read previous coverage:
 GoFundMe is investigating Lexi Thomas, Howard County woman accused of faking cancer
 Nov 14, 2026 She chronicled her struggle with cancer. Her husband said it was all made up.
 Oct 24, 2026 A podcast series released this autumn, “ The Lexi Con ,” accuses Thomas of conducting an elaborate scheme to convince family, friends and fellow church members she had blood cancer and was taking part in a study at the National Institutes of Health. 
 Podcast producers Nancy Moscatiello and Scott Eldridge, who also created the “Scamanda” podcast and docuseries about a California cancer faker, spent three years investigating Thomas. 
 Former friends and family members allege on the podcast that Thomas claimed her medical trial was so sensitive no one could accompany her on treatments, though she often brought her dog along. 
 They claim Thomas fabricated communications from members of her purported medical team, including Dr. Anthony Fauci, former chief medical adviser to President Joe Biden. 
 Advertise with us Guests on the podcast allege Thomas conducted numerous fundraisers, both online and in person, to cover the costs of her treatments and convinced several older adults to include her in their wills. 
 Moscatiello said Thursday she was “excited” to see the Thomas case move forward. 
 “The community deserves some kind of accountability and this is a first step,” she said, adding that she thought it was likely additional charges would be brought against Thomas. 
 “There are more things that she needs to be held accountable for,” she said.
 Among those alleged in the indictment to be victims of Thomas’ scheme are her sister and brother-in-law, Meghan and Dan Goldsmith, who have spoken extensively on the podcast. The parents of Thomas’ estranged husband are listed as victims. 
 Advertise with us A spokesperson for the GoFundMe platform confirmed last week that it was investigating Thomas. 
 Last month, Thomas’ husband, Gavin Hannan, filed for an annulment, claiming in court papers that he learned last year that she “did not, and never did, have cancer.” 
 “The doctors that Defendant [Thomas] claimed had saved her life, and treated her for years, have no record of her ever being a patient,” Hannan wrote in the filing. 
 The annulment filing and the podcast claim Thomas pasted her face onto photos of cancer patients to create blog and social media posts in which she detailed her treatments. 
 Hannan wrote in court records that, when he confronted Thomas, she “claimed to be suicidal and required hospitalization.”
 Advertise with us The Goldsmiths said in a statement that they were “deeply grateful” to police and prosecutors ”for their extensive work over the past 15 months as they have sought the truth in this complex case.”
 “Our sincere hope is that the hundreds of donors who supported Lexi’s fundraising will be made whole, and that this case makes clear that exploiting the generosity of others has consequences,” they wrote. “For once, she is exactly where she is supposed to be.” 
 Howard County Police did not immediately respond to requests for comment. A state’s attorney’s spokeswoman said the office had no further comment. 
 Thomas is scheduled for an initial appearance in Howard County Circuit Court on Dec. 2.
 This article may be updated. 
 Baltimore Banner reporter Lillian Reed contributed to this article. 
 Julie Scharper
